name: Civil Court (Junior Division)
description: First-instance civil court for smaller-value civil disputes -- money recovery, contract, small property matters.
notes: Pecuniary jurisdiction limits are set by each state government and vary widely -- verify the current limit in your district.

name: Civil Court (Senior Division) / District Judge
description: Civil court for higher-value civil disputes, and first appellate court for Junior Division decrees.
notes: Pecuniary jurisdiction limits are set by each state government and vary widely -- verify the current limit in your district.

name: Judicial Magistrate (First Class)
description: First-instance criminal court for most cognizable/non-cognizable offences short of the most serious ones.
notes: Sentencing powers are capped by law (typically up to 3 years' imprisonment) -- more serious offences are tried directly by Sessions Court.

name: Sessions Court
description: Tries serious criminal offences and hears appeals from Magistrate courts.

name: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
description: First-instance forum for consumer complaints about defective goods, deficient services, or unfair trade practices.
notes: Limit reflects the Consumer Protection Act 2019's July 2020 notification (up to ₹1 crore) -- verify the current limit before filing.

name: State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
description: Appeals from District Commissions, and first-instance forum for higher-value consumer complaints.
notes: Limit reflects the Consumer Protection Act 2019's July 2020 notification (₹1 crore to ₹10 crore) -- verify the current limit before filing.

name: National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
description: Appeals from State Commissions, and first-instance forum for the highest-value consumer complaints.
notes: Limit reflects the Consumer Protection Act 2019's July 2020 notification (above ₹10 crore) -- verify the current limit before filing.

name: Family Court
description: Matrimonial and family disputes -- divorce, judicial separation, maintenance, custody, guardianship.
notes: Not every district has a dedicated Family Court -- where absent, a designated Civil Court exercises this jurisdiction instead.

name: Labour Court
description: Individual employment disputes -- wrongful dismissal, wage disputes, service conditions for workmen.
notes: A labour dispute usually must first be raised via conciliation with the Labour Department before it can be referred here.

name: Industrial Tribunal
description: Collective/industrial disputes -- retrenchment, closure, collective bargaining disputes, larger-scale industrial matters.

name: Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT)
description: Service matters of central government employees -- recruitment, promotion, disciplinary action, pension.
notes: Has benches across states -- file at the bench with jurisdiction over the relevant government office.

name: Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT)
description: Recovery of debts owed to banks/financial institutions above the statutory threshold.
notes: Threshold (commonly cited around ₹20 lakh) is set by the Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act and can change by amendment -- verify the current figure.

name: Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT)
description: Appeals against orders of income tax authorities (Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals)).

name: National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
description: Company law and insolvency matters -- oppression/mismanagement, insolvency resolution (IBC), company disputes.
notes: Has benches across states -- file at the bench with jurisdiction over the company's registered office.

name: National Green Tribunal (NGT)
description: Environmental disputes -- pollution, forest and environmental clearance violations, compensation for environmental damage.
notes: Has a principal bench and zonal benches -- file at the zonal bench with jurisdiction over the affected area.

name: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT)
description: Compensation claims arising from motor vehicle accidents -- injury, death, or property damage.

name: Rent Control Court / Rent Authority
description: Landlord-tenant disputes -- eviction, rent fixation, tenancy renewal, under the applicable state rent control law.
notes: Rent control law, and whether a dedicated Rent Authority even exists, varies significantly by state -- verify locally.

name: High Court (Writ Jurisdiction)
description: Constitutional writs (habeas corpus, mandamus, certiorari, prohibition, quo warranto) for enforcement of fundamental rights or against government/authority action; also hears civil, criminal, and other appeals.

name: Supreme Court of India
description: Apex constitutional court -- final appeals, Special Leave Petitions, and writs under Article 32 for enforcement of fundamental rights.
notes: Ordinarily approached only after exhausting the High Court, except for a direct Article 32 writ petition.

name: Arbitral Tribunal (private arbitration)
description: Private dispute resolution under an arbitration clause/agreement, governed by the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 -- not a government court.
appealsTo: Court under Section 34 (limited grounds to set aside an award)
notes: Only available where the parties have an arbitration agreement/clause -- cannot be unilaterally invoked otherwise.

name: Police Station (FIR / Complaint)
description: Not an adjudicating forum -- the administrative starting point for a criminal matter: registering an FIR or a non-cognizable complaint.
appealsTo: Judicial Magistrate (if a valid FIR is refused, a complaint can be made to the Magistrate instead)

name: State / National Human Rights Commission
description: Investigates complaints of human rights violations by public servants/authorities and can recommend compensation or action; not a court, and its recommendations are not directly enforceable like a decree.
notes: Complementary to, not a substitute for, a court -- for binding, enforceable relief a writ petition to the High Court is usually still needed alongside or after an NHRC/SHRC complaint.

name: Central / State Information Commission
description: Second appellate authority for a Right to Information Act request that a public authority refused or didn't respond to within the statutory time limit.
notes: A first appeal must ordinarily be made to the public authority's own designated First Appellate Authority before approaching the Commission.

name: Gram Nyayalaya
description: Village/taluk-level court for petty civil and criminal matters, offering faster, informal, local access to justice.
notes: Not yet established in every state/district -- check whether one is functional in the relevant area.
